newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Gucci Q3 net revenues up 69 pct.
newsitem.headline: Gucci Q3 net revenues up 69 pct.

text.p: Luxury goods maker Gucci Group said on Thursday its third quarter net revenues were up 69.1 percent to $230.2 million from $136.1 million in the third quarter fiscal 1995.
Year-to-date, total net revenues reached $620.2 million, an 81.2 percent increase over the same period of fiscal 1995.

During the third quarter, sales through directly operated stores increased 64.9 percent, while wholesale sales (franchise, duty free, and speciality store distribution) were up 110.8 percent compared with the third quarter of the last year.
Leathergoods and shoes were the strongest product categories, with sales rising 94.7 percent and 68.9 percent, respectively.

"Our customers responded very well to our Fall/Winter 1997 collections. We are pleased with the order portfolio for the Cruise and Spring/Summer 1997 collections," said Domenico De Sole, President and Chief Executive Officer of the group quoted on both the Amsterdam and New York stock exchanges.
"We believe the strong consumer response, combined with our focus on improving systems and achieving efficiencies, position us well for the fourth quarter."
"Our plan for the refurbishment and expansion of our stores, as well as new openings, remains on track. This month, we will open a new store in Berlin," De Sole said.
"In 1997, we will roll out our new store concept with the refurbishment of several key locations including Beverly Hills, Dallas and London, Sloane Street."
"We expect these programmes to result in greater store productivity, while enhancing the Gucci image."
